accuracy.evidence: Word list and definitions match CCSS L.K.1e (most frequently occurring prepositions: to, from, in, out, on, off, for, of, by, with) and L.1.1i; the England national curriculum places position and direction language in Year 1 mathematics and prepositions for place in Year 3 English (Appendix 2). Every lab instruction was checked against its zone: 'in' only accepts inside the basket, 'next to' only beside it, 'off the log' only the grass, 'into' only inside the pond ellipse.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early-years confusions: in versus on (first prediction and SLIP messages), under versus in, next to versus on, off read only as a switch (frog prediction 'Still on the log'), and to versus from (opposites step and challenge 'from' feedback). Each wrong drop names where the thing actually landed and what the asked-for word means.

lab_distinct.evidence: Built around prepositions themselves: a drag-to-zone scene where the drop position is classified as on/under/in/next to, a reverse naming task with the same scene, an opposites matcher, a direction scene with a pond ellipse and log for off/into/out of/to, and a three-item tidy-up that follows spoken phrases. Passed the 30% shingle gate; no other flagship has a spatial-zone classifier.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child first acts out each position word, then reverses the skill by naming a position, then meets the words as opposite pairs, then moves from where-words to which-way words with a moving frog, and finally follows real two-part instructions, the CCSS evidence 'Follow instructions involving prepositions'.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'The cat is on the table: inside the table' (the cat must go on top), 'Opposite of on: in' (on pairs with off), and 'Hop off the log: still on the log' (the frog must land on the grass).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with twelve distinct m= messages that each name the slip: under versus on, in versus on for a hat, out of versus into, under the pool, on and to mistaken for opposites of up, on top versus under, inside versus under, from versus to, off versus to, and naming a thing instead of the position words.

readability.evidence: Kid text is short read-aloud sentences with concrete objects (mat, bed, bowl, frog, log) within the family kid limit; adult text names the standards and is within 10.0. Canvas instructions are one short phrase in large type, and buttons pair an emoji with one or two words.

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler regex and 12% duplicate gate. Kid paragraphs cover position words, next to, direction words, and opposite pairs; adult paragraphs cover standards, prepositional phrases and contrast pairs, named mistakes, and what the lab does; the family tip is one 'Teddy says' game.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px light, iPhone 13 dark, and mid-task and finished screenshots for every step: table, basket, pond, bed and box scale with the canvas; emoji targets are about 34 px with a 30 px minimum grab radius; instruction text is large and inside the canvas; nothing clipped.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13, every task completed by Show me, no console errors. Every drag has a button route (cat place buttons, word buttons, pair buttons, frog grass/pond/flower buttons, tidy place buttons); the canvas aria-label states the current instruction and the result of each move.
